prompt: What does God create on the sixth day, completing his work of creation?
options: Land animals and humankind, in his own image
The sun, moon, and stars
The birds and sea creatures
The dry land and the seas

prompt: What do Adam and Eve do immediately after eating the forbidden fruit?
options: They realize they are naked and sew fig leaves together to cover themselves
They immediately die a physical death
They ask God to curse the serpent immediately, before he ever speaks a word to either of them
They build an altar to atone for their sin

prompt: Why does God decide to send a flood over the earth?
options: Because human wickedness and violence on the earth have become great and continual
Because Cain murdered Abel, and the shed blood cries out from the ground for judgment
Because a tower was being built to reach the heavens
Because Pharaoh refused to release Israel

prompt: What does God do after the people build a tower at Babel to make a name for themselves?
options: He confuses their language and scatters them across the earth
He destroys the tower with fire sent down from heaven before anyone can finish building it
He turns the builders into pillars of salt

A son through his wife Sarai
Protection from four invading kings
A written copy of the covenant terms, signed and witnessed by the elders of his household

prompt: What does God provide as a substitute after Abraham binds Isaac on the altar?
options: A ram caught by its horns in a thicket
A lamb from Abraham's own flock
Nothing; Isaac is spared with no substitute offered
A dove Abraham brought from home

prompt: How does Jacob trick his father Isaac into giving him Esau's blessing?
options: He wears goatskins on his arms and neck and brings in a meal, pretending to be Esau
He forges a written blessing while Isaac sleeps
He bribes Esau to give up the blessing voluntarily

prompt: What does the man Jacob wrestles with all night do just before letting him go at daybreak?

He blesses Jacob's flocks and servants
He tells Jacob to return to Laban
He gives Jacob a new set of laws

prompt: What do Joseph's brothers do to him after he arrives to check on them wearing his colorful robe?
options: They strip him, throw him into a pit, and sell him to traders heading to Egypt
They kill him on the spot and tell their father a wild animal must have devoured him
They send him home to their father in disgrace
They make him a servant in their own tents

prompt: What does Joseph do that leads Pharaoh to put him in charge of Egypt?
options: He interprets Pharaoh's dreams and proposes storing grain for the coming famine
He defeats Egypt's enemies in battle
He marries into Pharaoh's family
He builds monuments and temples as tribute to Pharaoh's household and its many gods

prompt: What does Joseph do when he finally reveals his identity to his brothers?
options: He weeps aloud, tells them he is Joseph, and sends for their father
He has them arrested for their earlier crime
He demands they return the money they paid for grain
He refuses to speak to them and sends them away

prompt: How does the book of Genesis end?
options: With Joseph's death in Egypt and his request that his bones be carried to the promised land one day
With Jacob's burial in Egypt and no further mention of the promise
With Joseph appointing one of his own two sons as his successor to continue ruling Egypt after him
With Joseph's brothers returning permanently to Canaan without him

prompt: What does Noah do after planting a vineyard, setting off the incident that leads to Canaan being cursed?
options: He drinks its wine, becomes drunk, and lies uncovered in his tent
He offers its first fruits to God at an altar
He refuses to drink from it and destroys the vineyard
He gives the entire vineyard to Shem alone

prompt: What happens to Lot's wife as the family flees the destruction of Sodom?
options: She looks back and turns into a pillar of salt
She dies in the fire that destroys the city
She refuses to leave and stays behind
She leads her daughters safely to Zoar

prompt: What sign does God give as a reminder of his covenant not to flood the earth again?
options: A rainbow
A burning bush
A pillar of cloud
A dove

prompt: What threefold promise does God make when he first calls Abram?
options: Wealth, fame, and a large army
Land, descendants, and blessing to the nations
Long life, health, and peace
A new language and a new name

prompt: How does Abram respond when God promises him offspring as numerous as the stars?

He doubts and walks away
He believes God, and it is credited to him as righteousness
He asks for the promise to be given to Lot instead

prompt: What new sign does God introduce as the mark of his covenant with Abraham's household?

Sacrifice of a firstborn son
Wearing special garments
Building a temple

prompt: What name changes accompany the covenant of circumcision?
options: Isaac becomes Israel
Abram and Sarai become Abraham and Sarah
Jacob becomes Abraham
Abram becomes Abraham while Sarai keeps her own name

God repeats the promise of numerous offspring and blessing to the nations
God requires an additional sacrifice from Isaac

prompt: How does God confirm the covenant promise to Isaac?

By repeating to Isaac the same promises made to Abraham

By requiring Isaac to build an altar in Egypt

prompt: What does God promise Jacob in his dream at Bethel?
options: To abandon him if he leaves Canaan
To be with him, protect him, and bring him back to the land
To give the land to Esau instead

prompt: What does the name Israel, given to Jacob at Peniel, become for the people descended from him?
options: A curse on his family
The name of the nation that will come from him
A title reserved only for Jacob himself
A rejection of God's earlier promises

prompt: What ritual accompanies God's covenant-making with Abram, and what does it signify?
options: A smoking fire pot and flaming torch pass between the pieces, signifying God alone takes on the obligation
Abram and God pass between the pieces together, signifying that the two of them take on matching obligations
A rainbow appears over the animals

They exchange sons as hostages

prompt: Besides the later sign of the rainbow, what commitment does God make to Noah after the flood?

A command to never eat meat

A ban on building cities

prompt: Who besides Abraham's direct line is included in the covenant sign of circumcision?
options: Only Isaac
Every male in Abraham's household, including servants
No one but Abraham himself

prompt: What happens at Bethel when Jacob returns there in obedience to God?
options: God renames him Israel again and reaffirms the covenant blessing
God transfers the covenant blessing from Jacob to his firstborn son Reuben
Jacob builds a permanent temple
Esau joins Jacob in worship there

prompt: What does Cain say to God after being sentenced to wander the earth for killing Abel?
options: "My punishment is greater than I can bear"
"I am willing to accept whatever punishment you give"
"Please forgive me and restore Abel to life"
He says nothing and walks away silently

prompt: What does Genesis say about Noah, in contrast to the rest of his generation, just before the flood?

prompt: What does Abram do when God tells him to leave his country, his people, and his father's household?

He refuses and stays behind in Haran, unwilling to leave everything familiar to his father's household

Continue on to Egypt where her family will take her in
Wait in the wilderness until Sarai comes looking for her

"I no longer believe God keeps his promises"
"This child belongs to Hagar, not to me"

prompt: What does Esau do when he comes in from the field exhausted and smells Jacob's stew?
options: He sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew and some bread
He refuses to trade and insists on hunting his own food instead of trading anything away

He marries Rachel to another man first
He refuses to let Jacob marry either daughter

Because Joseph reports them to Pharaoh for a crime
Because Joseph is the firstborn and inherits everything

prompt: How does Joseph respond when Potiphar's wife tries to seduce him?

He gives in to avoid conflict
He reports her to Pharaoh immediately
He flees Egypt entirely

prompt: What does Judah offer to do when Joseph threatens to keep Benjamin as a slave?

prompt: How loudly does Joseph weep when he finally reveals himself to his brothers?

Quietly, so that only his brothers hear

prompt: What is Jacob doing when he gathers his twelve sons before his death?

prompt: What does God do to prevent Adam and Eve from returning to the garden of Eden after expelling them?

prompt: Why does Cain kill his brother Abel?

Abel steals Cain's inheritance

prompt: What does God promise will happen to "all the families of the earth" when he first calls Abram?

prompt: What does Abraham name the place where God provides the ram in place of Isaac?

prompt: What does God call his completed work, at the end of the six days of creation?

prompt: What two dreams does Joseph tell his brothers about, provoking their hatred?

prompt: Where does Abram's father Terah settle the family on their way from Ur to Canaan?

Egypt
Beersheba
